thread:
alex: FYI queue depth for model/reddo-13b in us-west-2 spiked — per-shard backlog ~18k, sustained ~12m.
infra-bot: alert: queue_depth_threshold_exceeded model=reddo-13b region=us-west-2 value=18342 severity=high
maya: seeing the same in grafana, tail latency 4x normal. origin looks concentrated on 2 hot shards.
joel: tagging @sre @capacity — what's current spare GPU count in usw2?
anjali: free GPUs in pool = 2 (non-preemptible). We have 6 reserved for dedicated customers that we can't reclaim instantly.
sara: quick correlate with traffic logs: a single client (billing-gen) started a ramp and is streaming many short prompts -> high prefix reuse but per-request KV miss due to sharding mismatch.
alex: so it's a hotshard + a large streaming client. Can we short-circuit streaming requests to a cheaper variant temporarily?
maya: we should do two things: (1) apply emergency per-model admission limits, (2) route non-critical requests to reddo-7b.
joel: agree. also think about temporary eviction of large cache entries for that model to free memory and allow more in-flight requests.
anjali: I can push a rate-limit change and a routing override. Proposed admission change: cap reddo-13b QPS to 30% of current for 10m, then evaluate.
sara: +1. For routing: add a rule on the model-router to send requests with tag `fallback=true` or requests without streaming to reddo-7b. Most of billing-gen calls are non-streaming.
alex: can someone run the quick patch? here's the k8s patch we used last time to flip per-model throttles:
```
kubectl patch configmap admission -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"per_model_throttle.reddo-13b":"0.3"}}'
```
anjali: applying now. will also push a router override via api-gateway with low TTL.
infra-bot: deploy started by anjali [deploy-1912345722]
maya: watching metrics. if per-shard backlog drops below 2k within 6m we can start progressive ramp-up.
joel: I patched an emergency autoscale policy to allow one burst node (preemptible) if CPU < 40% and GPU mem free > 20%. this buys ~4 replicas for short window.
sara: note: billing-gen is on a managed customer plan; we should message CSM before any hard throttling beyond 50%. I'll ping @cs-rep.
alex: good call. keep throttles conservative for now. priority: reduce queue depth and avoid OOMs on shard hosts.
anjali: router override and throttle applied. infra-bot shows rollout ok.
infra-bot: router-rule-updated route=reddo-fallback criteria=(non_streaming or header:fallback) by=anjali
maya: metrics trending down — backlog per-shard now 9.1k and falling. tail latency improving.
joel: still seeing a couple of nodes with high swap churn. I'm kicking a targeted cache-evict on those hosts: `/usr/local/bin/kv-evict --model=reddo-13b --percent=20 --host=usw2-node-23`
sara: CSM notified the customer about possible degraded throughput and fallback routing. they acknowledged.
alex: rough timeline and owners: (1) immediate throttle + routing — anjali (done), (2) temporary preemptible scale — joel (in progress), (3) cache eviction sweep — joel (in progress), (4) customer comms — sara (ack).
maya: we'll keep this thread for postmortem notes. if backlog stays <2k for 30m, we close.
infra-bot: incident note appended to channel incident-log id=INC-2026-1912345678
alex: thanks all. follow-up: add a short runbook for hotshard incidents (admission quick commands, router toggles, eviction script).
anjali: putting a draft runbook in #eng-infra/playbooks in 30m.
maya: closing check: last backlog sample 1,820 per shard. marking recovery in 10m unless regressions. :white_check_mark:
